exposure: uterine fibroid size/diameter (< 5 cm, 5-10 cm, > 10 cm)
cohort: The study included 651 pregnant women with sonographically confirmed uterine fibroids.
finding: Fibroid diameter, particularly lesions > 5 cm and especially > 10 cm, was a key determinant of obstetric and neonatal risk, leading to markedly increased rates of maternal haemorrhage, preterm birth, and neonatal morbidity.
mod_finding: Caesarean delivery rates increased stepwise with fibroid size, from 56.6% for fibroids < 5 cm to 92.1% for fibroids > 10 cm.
